This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. This petition under Section 482 Cr.PC is filed by accused nos.1 to 3 with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in Crime No.19/2024 registered by Vijayanagara Police Station, Bengaluru City,
for the offences punishable under Sections 498A & 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Manoj.

2 Prohibition NC: 2024:KHC:15154 Act, 1961, which is now pending before the Court of XXIV Addl.
Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru.

2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
3. Learned Counsel for the petitioners and the learned Counsel for respondent no.2 jointly submit that the dispute between the parties has been amicably settled.

The parties have filed IA-2/2024 before this Court under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Cr.PC with a prayer to permit the parties to compound the offences for which FIR has been registered against the petitioners herein.
4. The application filed by the parties under Section 320 read with Section 482 Cr.PC which is supported by the affidavit of respondent no.2 is taken on record.

In paragraph 2 to 4 of the application, it is stated as under:
"2.

The petitioners and respondent no.2 submit that at the intervention of well-wishers the petitioner and respondent no.2 and accused no.1 are intending to compound the case and the respondent no.2 is not intending to proceed further with the case against the petitioner.

Petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 had filed a divorce petition under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act in M.C.No.1111/2024 before the Hon'ble IV Additional Principal Family Judge at Bengaluru for dissolution of marriage, wherein the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 appeared before the mediation and matter had been settled between the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2.

entities.text: Additional Principal Family Judge at Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In terms of the settlement, the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have agreed mutually that petitioner no.1 agreed to pay a permanent alimony of Rs.14,00,000/- other than that the parties have no other claims against each other either past, present or future as both of them are employed and have further agreed that they shall not interfere with each other's lives and they shall not interfere in personal and professional lives.
a) In terms of the settlement, the  petitioner no.1 had paid an amount of Rs.7,00,000/- to the respondent no.2 on the day of filing of the divorce petition.
b) The petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay the amount of Rs.7,00,000/- on the day of dissolution of marriage.
4. The respondent no.2 further submits that there is no coercion or compulsion on her to compound the offence, but on her own freewill agreed to compound the case.

Hence this application seeking kind permission of this Hon'ble Court to compound the offences."

sentences.text:
In paragraph 2 of the affidavit filed by respondent no.2 in support of the application, it is stated as under:
"2. I state that, I have settled the issues with the petitioners amicably and I have no objection to quash the proceedings in Crime No.19/2024 for offences punishable under Sections 498A of IPC and Section 3 & 4 of D.P.Act on the file of 24th Addl.
CMM, Nrupathunga Road, Bengaluru."
6.
The parties who are present before the Court are identified by their learned advocates.

On enquiry, respondent no.2 and her advocate have admitted that respondent no.2 has received a sum of Rs.7 lakhs from petitioner no.1 and it is also stated that the balance amount of Rs.7 lakhs shall be paid to respondent no.2 before the Family Court in M.C.No.1111/2024.
7.
The dispute involved in the case is between the members of the family and at the intervention of well-wishers and elders of both the families, the dispute has been amicable settled.
The alleged offences are compoundable in nature.
Considering the nature of settlement arrived, the prayer made in the application as well as the in the main petition is required to be allowed.

Accordingly, the following order:
NC: 2024:KHC:15154 8. IA-2/2024 is allowed.
The parties are permitted to compound the offences for which FIR has been registered against the petitioners in Crime No.19/2024.
Consequently, petition is allowed.

The entire proceedings in Crime No.19/2024 registered by Vijayanagara Police Station, Bengaluru City,
for the offences punishable under Sections 498A & 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, which is now pending before the Court of XXIV Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, is hereby quashed.
